Each research area below is a separate modular folder. Edit its index.qmd metadata to change the title, subtitle, summary, image, or ordering.














DNA Crystal Engineering


Programming periodic matter from nucleic acids


Design, assembly, topology, and structural analysis of three-dimensional DNA crystals.












Metal-Mediated Nucleic Acids


Coordination chemistry inside programmable biomolecular systems


Metal-directed structures, transmetalation, catalysis, and molecular electronic function.












Programmable Hybrid Materials


Translating molecular information into inorganic structure


DNA-directed mineralization, replication, coating, and fabrication of hybrid materials.












Origins and Catalysis


Metal–nucleic-acid interactions before modern biology


Exploring how simple nucleic-acid and metal assemblies could support structure and catalysis.

title: Vecchioni Lab
text:
A Metal Design Language
The overarching theme of the Lab is to develop a bioinorganic programming language in which topological self-assembly of nucleic acids is carried out using metal base pairs. By replacing select hydrogen bonds with metal coordination bonds, we aim to expand the intrinsic functionality of nucleic acids to interface with light, electrons, and biochemical inputs.
Using high-throughput X-ray crystallography, iterative design, and collaboration with chemists and physicists, we aim to make molecules, such as the 3D tile shown here, possible in the near future.
Explore this research →

title: Vecchioni Lab
text:
Molecular Electronics and Quantum Materials
We use DNA to organize metals and molecular components with atomic precision, exploring how programmable structure can give rise to electronic, magnetic, and quantum phenomena.
Explore this research →

title: Vecchioni Lab
text:
Nanophotonics in DNA
We use programmable nucleic-acid architectures to organize optical components with nanoscale precision, creating materials in which structure controls the interaction of light and matter.
Explore this research →

title: Vecchioni Lab
text:
(A)Biomorphogenesis
We explore how molecular information propagates across length scales to generate form, using DNA to build and study crystalline, topological, inorganic, and hybrid materials.
Explore this research →

title: Vecchioni Lab
text:
Origins of Life and Astrobiology
We investigate how interactions between nucleic acids, metals, and self-assembling molecular systems could have contributed to the emergence of structure, function, and catalysis in early chemical evolution.
Explore this research →

title: Vecchioni Lab
text:
Building Community
We build tools, databases, shared resources, and scientific communities that make nucleic-acid materials research more accessible, reproducible, and collaborative.
